title: Road Trip Diary, Day One
text:
Today we started our road trip to Aunt Bea's farm. Dad packed two suitcases, a cooler, and {number} {plural noun}, just in case.

Mom held the map. She said to turn left at the big {noun} and drive {adverb} until we saw a sign for {place}. My little brother Theo sang a song about {plural noun} the whole way.

For lunch we stopped at a picnic table by a lake. I ate a sandwich with {food} in the middle. Dad said it was the most {adjective} sandwich he had ever seen.

At night we stayed at a hotel with a pool shaped like a {noun}. Theo and I {past tense verb} in the water until our {plural noun} got wrinkly. Aunt Bea says tomorrow we get to {verb} with her {adjective} goats.

title: Greetings from Echo Canyon
text:
Dear Grandpa, greetings from Echo Canyon! We drove here in Mom's blue car. It took {number} hours, and we only stopped once to look at a {adjective} cow.

The canyon is deep and orange. When you yell into it, it yells back. I yelled "{silly word}!" and the canyon yelled it back {adverb}. A ranger named Mr. Hall told us the rocks are millions of years old and mostly made of {plural noun}.

Today we hiked on a flat, safe trail. Dad wore his big hat with a {noun} on top. We saw a lizard {verb ending in ing} on a warm rock. Then it {past tense verb} away.

I bought you a present at the gift shop. It is a tiny {noun} in a glass jar, so please keep it somewhere {adjective}. Tomorrow we will {verb} at the visitor center and eat {food} for lunch. Love, June, your {adjective} granddaughter

title: Rules for the Back Seat Spotting Game
text:
This is the official spotting game for our family van. Everyone in the back seat can play. Grown-ups who are driving may not play, because they need to watch the road.

When you see a red car, shout "{exclamation}!" and get one point. When you see a {adjective} dog with its head out the window, you get two points. A truck carrying {plural noun} is five points. If you spot a cow wearing a {noun}, you win right away.

You may not {verb} while you are spotting. Keep your {body part} inside the car at all times. If you yell too {adverb}, you lose a point, and Mom will give you a {adjective} look. If two people tie, the winner is whoever can {verb} the longest.

Last week my sister won. She {past tense verb} all the way home and picked a song about {verb ending in ing} {plural noun}. We listened to it {number} times.

title: Snacks Packed for the Long Drive
text:
Mom made a snack list for our drive to the beach. She wrote it in {color} crayon and taped it to the cooler.

The front pocket has apple slices, cheese sticks, and a bag of {adjective} {plural noun}. The cooler has water bottles, yogurt cups, and one big jar of {food} for Dad. Dad says he needs it to drive {adverb}.

The secret bag under my seat has crackers shaped like a {noun} and {number} {plural noun} from Grandma. Grandma says to only open it if somebody starts {verb ending in ing}.

The snack rules are on the back. Please do not {verb} with your food. Crumbs must stay in the car, not in your {noun}. Juice boxes must be squeezed {adverb}. Whoever finishes first has to tell a story about a {adjective} sandwich.

title: Things Dad Packed in the Trunk
text:
Before every trip, Dad makes a list of everything in the trunk. He says a good traveler is a {adjective} traveler. Here is his list for this year.

One tent, folded very flat. Two sleeping bags that smell a little bit like {food}. One spare tire and a box of {plural noun} for emergencies. A pillow for Mom, a {adjective} blanket for me, and a tiny {noun} for my baby sister. Last of all, his lucky {noun}. Dad has brought it on every trip since he was {number} years old. He says it helps him {verb} when the road is bumpy.

At the very bottom is a mystery box. When I shook it, it went "{sound}!" and something inside {past tense verb}. Mom just smiled {adverb}.

At the campsite, Dad finally opened the box. Inside was a big pile of {plural noun}. Dad says that is what every {adjective} camper needs.

title: Welcome to the Sunny Hills Rest Stop
text:
Welcome to the Sunny Hills Rest Stop! We are happy you stopped to stretch your legs. Please read these signs before you explore.

Our picnic tables are painted {color} and are perfect for eating {plural noun}. The water fountain is next to the big {noun}. It works best if you ask it {adverb}.

The dog area is behind the fence. Dogs may sniff, run, and {verb}, but they may not chase the {plural noun}. A friendly {animal} named Biscuit lives by the gate. Biscuit enjoys {verb ending in ing} and being told he is {adjective}.

The gift shop sells maps, hats, and a snow globe with a tiny {noun} inside. Our best seller is a T-shirt that says "I Stopped at Sunny Hills and All I Got Was a {adjective} {noun}." Thank you for visiting. Please wave {adverb} as you drive away.

title: The Traffic Report on Radio Five
text:
Good morning, drivers! This is Penny Park with the traffic report from Radio Five. Main Street is slow today because a farmer is walking {number} {plural noun} across the road. Please wait {adverb} and wave hello.

On the highway, a truck full of {food} is stuck behind a {adjective} tractor. Over on Oak Bridge, a man is {verb ending in ing} in a {adjective} costume. He waves at every car. At the car wash, there is a long line of {plural noun} waiting to get clean.

The weather today is sunny with a small chance of {plural noun} in the afternoon. A hot air balloon {past tense verb} over the school this morning. If you are going to the lake, bring sunglasses and a {noun}.

That is all for now. Buckle up, drive {adverb}, and remember to {verb} every time you see a yellow car!

title: Dear Grandma, We Are Almost There
text:
Dear Grandma, we are on our way to your house! I am writing in the back seat, so sorry if my letters are wiggly. We have been driving for {number} hours. So far I have counted seven horses, two windmills, and one very {adjective} {noun}.

Dad keeps singing the same song about {plural noun}. Mom says if he sings it one more time, she will {verb}. My cousin Sam is asleep and {verb ending in ing} with his mouth open. He is hugging his {noun} like a teddy bear.

We stopped for lunch at a diner. My grilled cheese came with a side of {plural noun}. The waiter said it was the house special and bowed {adverb}. Dessert was pie with {food} on top.

Please get the guest room ready. I am bringing my pillow, my toothbrush, and a {adjective} surprise. I think it will make you {verb}. Love, Maya
P.S. Please tell your cat I said "{silly word}."

title: Mom's Directions to the Campground
text:
These are Mom's directions to Pine Tree Campground. Read them to the driver one step at a time.

First, turn right at the house with the {adjective} mailbox. Keep going until you see a gas station shaped like a {noun}. Wave at the man who sells {plural noun} on the corner. He always waves back with his {body part}.

Next, get on the long road and stay on it for {number} miles. You will pass a field full of {plural noun}. Do not stop to look at them, or we will be late for dinner.

When you see a sign with a picture of a {animal} wearing sunglasses, turn left. The road gets bumpy here, so drive {adverb} and hold on to your {noun}. If the baby starts {verb ending in ing}, sing the song about the {adjective} bus.

At the campground, find the ranger named Lou. Tell him our family is here to {verb}. He will give us a map and a {adjective} welcome.

title: Rules for Riding in the Family Van
text:
Welcome to the Garcia family van. Every passenger must read these rules before we {verb}.

Rule one: Everyone buckles up, even the {animal}. Rule two: Feet stay on the floor, not on your brother's {body part}. Rule three: The window may only be opened if you ask {adverb}.

Rule four: Nobody is allowed to {verb} until we get to the highway. Rule five: If you need a break, say the magic word, which is "{silly word}." Rule six: Snacks must be shared. Last time, Abuela brought a {adjective} bag of {plural noun} and gave the biggest one to the dog. Rule seven: Singing is allowed, but loud {verb ending in ing} is only allowed on Saturdays.

Rule eight: The driver is in charge, and today the driver is Papa. He has driven this van for {number} years and has only gotten lost in a {noun} once. Last summer he {past tense verb} the whole way to the lake. Please give him a {adjective} round of applause.
